hook: You feel your stomach flutter when a story ends with a twist.

sections.title: Story
sections.narration: You feel your stomach flutter when a story ends with a twist. That flutter is actually your brain rewarding prediction errors. In 1994, neuroscientist Antonio Damasio reported about a 30 percent faster decision when gut feelings were involved. What does your gut actually tell you? It signals that something unexpected just happened. The result? Later research by Wolfram Schultz in 1997 showed dopamine spikes about 50 percent higher during unexpected outcomes, confirming the prediction error theory. So why do we assume a story can change your stomach? Because the brain treats narrative surprise like a real reward, triggering the same gut response. Do children experience the same reaction? Yes, studies show they do across ages. Kids reacting to surprising endings illustrate this effect across cultures and ages. Other societies, from medieval storytellers to modern gamers, show similar physiological spikes. That's it. That link shows how stories shape our emotions from the inside out. Understanding this helps you see why kids love plot twists so much.
